bullets.title: Fed hike odds spike to 70%+ as oil, PPI, and yields surge in tandem
bullets.body: CME FedWatch odds of a September FOMC hike rose above 70-73% on the day, with the 2-year Treasury surging 14bps to 4.57% and the 10-year rising 12bps to 4.96% — the highest since Oct 2023. Core PPI came in at +0.2% m/m (below the 0.3% forecast), but WTI crude's 8-session, ~20% rally to $102+/barrel driven by Houthi control of Bab el-Mandeb kept the hawkish narrative intact. S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted their fourth straight decline; the ECB is also expected to hike in October.

bullets.title: Tech CPI surge: DRAM +280% YoY, memory fully booked through 2027, pushing core inflation higher
bullets.body: AI hyperscaler capex exceeding $100B is driving a sustained component cost surge — DRAM prices up 280% YoY with analysts forecasting another 33% gain through mid-2027; NAND expected +21% over the same period. Global tech CPI contribution has swung from a -0.1%pt drag to a +0.1%pt boost, forecast to peak near 5% YoY in 1Q27. US PCE tech inflation printed 15% 3m/3m saar in July, and memory manufacturers are fully booked, reversing decades of tech deflation.

bullets.title: Oracle Q1 blows past estimates; books $30B AI cloud contracts, RPO balloons to $664B
bullets.body: ORCL reported Q1 revenue of $19.35B vs. $19.14B consensus, EPS $1.92 vs. $1.74, and operating margin of 42.1% vs. 40.7% consensus. The company booked over $30B in new AI cloud contracts in the quarter, pushing RPO to $664B (+$209B YoY), and delivered 300,000+ GPUs to cloud customers — nearly triple Q4 capacity. FY27 revenue guidance raised to $90B+ and EPS to $8.10; stock up ~7% after hours.

bullets.title: Adobe Q3 in-line; AI-first ARR >$650M growing 150%+ YoY, Q4 guide slightly light
bullets.body: ADBE reported Q3 revenue of $6.76B (vs. $6.69B est.) and EPS of $6.13 (vs. $6.08), with total ARR of $27.50B (+11.2% YoY). AI-first ARR exceeded $650M growing more than 150% YoY. FY revenue guidance raised to $26.576-26.626B, though Q4 revenue guide of $6.80-6.85B came in slightly below the $6.84B consensus.

bullets.title: Broad market sold off; semis -2.7% on DeepSeek memory-efficient model and DOJ probe into NVDA-Groq deal
bullets.body: The S&P 500 IT Index fell 0.9% and semis dropped 2.7% as DeepSeek launched a significantly lower-cost, memory-efficient AI model pressuring memory names. Separately, the DOJ opened an investigation into Nvidia's licensing deal with Groq, which allegedly was structured to avoid antitrust review. AAPL rebounded +3.6% from iPhone event weakness; META fell 1.4% despite a JPMorgan upgrade to Overweight.

bullets.title: Citi TMT conf broadly bullish on AI infrastructure buildout; management teams upbeat across hardware and networking
bullets.body: Management teams at Citi's 2026 Global TMT Conference were broadly comfortable with operating fundamentals, citing strong AI workload demand, opportunities for capital returns, and stabilizing wireless competition. Dell booked $61B in AI orders in Q2 with a $95B backlog and pipeline running multiples of backlog; enterprise AI customer base grew 60% in six months to 6,500+, with only 10-15% of enterprises having completed meaningful agentic AI modernization.

bullets.title: Arista raises 2026 revenue guidance to $12.6B (40% growth); AI cycle still has multi-year runway
bullets.body: ANET raised its 2026 revenue guidance to ~$12.6B at the Citi TMT Conference, with purchase commitments nearly tripling to $9.6B over three quarters. Scale-across networking is ~1/3 of AI sales and expanding; scale-up revenue (Ethernet) is excluded from 2026 guidance with pilots expected in 2027 and commercial revenue in 2028. Citi maintains Buy at $215 PT (36x 2028 EPS).

bullets.title: MSFT plans to triple data center capacity to 38GW by 2032 to meet AI/cloud demand
bullets.body: Microsoft announced plans to expand its data center footprint from 12GW to 38GW by 2032, driven by AI and cloud business demand growth. The expansion underscores the scale of hyperscaler capex commitments that are simultaneously fueling memory inflation and AI networking demand.

bullets.title: Cisco targets $7.5B AI revenue in FY27 on $9B+ hyperscaler orders; campus refresh adds $100B+ networking TAM
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on CSCO with a $139 PT (+29%), citing a $7.5B FY27 AI revenue target built on $9B+ AI orders in FY26 (60% Silicon One, 40% Acacia optics), design wins at three hyperscalers for the P200 chip with 90-day qualification cycles, and a $100B+ networking TAM from campus port refresh and data center modernization. Q1 FY27 is expected to be the gross margin trough due to high hardware mix; Silicon One is <10% of switches shipped today but expected to be majority by FY29.

bullets.title: GenAI search driving higher-intent traffic and better ad conversion; Citi incrementally positive on GOOGL
bullets.body: At Citi's TMT Conference, the GEO panel highlighted that LLM search queries average 20+ keywords vs. 2-3 in traditional search, targeting higher-intent users deeper in the purchase funnel with better conversion rates. Citi is incrementally positive on search ad demand and maintains Buy on GOOGL with a $447 PT (28x 2027E GAAP EPS of $15.72); Google Cloud is reaccelerating on TPU and Gemini demand.

bullets.title: Agentic AI framed as a structural enterprise security inflection; CrowdStrike and others positioning for durable spend increase
bullets.body: At the Goldman and Citi TMT conferences, CrowdStrike framed agentic AI as durably increasing security urgency — not a temporary tailwind. New products (SafeMind, Guardion) target AI/agent identity and exposure management; Flex-first GTM is designed to limit revenue cliffs. Separately, Island CEO noted that ~80% of observed enterprise AI prompts are non-productive and that traditional security architectures inspect less than 30% of enterprise traffic, pointing to a structural gap incumbents cannot close without platform reinvention.

bullets.title: Real estate sector underperforms as 10Y yields hit 4.96%; Fed hike odds weigh on REITs and towers
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Real Estate Index fell 0.87% as the 10-year Treasury rose 12bps to 4.96% and 30-year mortgage rates climbed to 7.07% — the highest since June 2025. Data centers and towers (down 1.69% YTD) lagged despite AI tailwinds. Single-family REITs (INVH, AMH) declined after disappointing rent growth updates.

bullets.title: Oil up 8 straight sessions (~+20%); Houthi Red Sea control and Saudi production cuts are the driver
bullets.body: WTI crude surged past $102/barrel — the eighth consecutive session of gains, up roughly 20% over the stretch — on Houthi control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait limiting Red Sea traffic, while Saudi oil production fell 1.9M bpd to its lowest since 1990. US diesel futures hit $5/gallon for the first time since April 2022. OPEC cut its 2026 global oil demand growth forecast to 380K bpd from 580K bpd.

bullets.title: 22V: US economy's speed limit ~1.75-2%; stronger demand likely forces tighter Fed path
bullets.body: 22V Chief Economist Gerard MacDonell argues the US economy's structural growth ceiling is around 1.75-2%, meaning stronger near-term demand does not translate to better medium-term growth. With the labor market near full employment and inflation above target, any demand strength increases the probability of a more restrictive Fed trajectory rather than accelerating real growth.

bullets.title: Key macro calendar next week: FOMC rate decision Sept 16, CPI tomorrow (Sept 11), China data Sept 14
bullets.body: JPMorgan's macro calendar flags the FOMC rate decision on September 16 at 2pm ET as the dominant event next week, with August CPI (due September 11) serving as the critical input for hike-or-hold. China Retail Sales and Industrial Production are due September 14. US Retail Sales and Housing Starts follow later in the week. META Connect is scheduled September 23-24; Xi's potential US visit also flagged for Sept 24.

bullets.title: META upgraded to Overweight at JPM and Wells Fargo on AI agents; PT raised to $820 at Wells
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded META to Overweight citing Models Agents deployment; Wells Fargo separately upgraded META to Overweight with a PT increase from $640 to $820, citing early-stage frontier AI model development and product opportunities beyond advertising. META declined 1.4% on the session despite the upgrades.

bullets.title: iPhone 18 subsidies rise to $1,200 (aligned with Apple's $100 price hike) but remain rational across carriers
bullets.body: JPM's telecom tracker finds T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon all offering up to $1,200 off the iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max with trade-in, matching Apple's price increase from the iPhone 17 cycle. Promotional discipline is described as intact; T-Mobile lowered its entry Essentials Saver plan to $30/month (from $50), matching Verizon's Simplicity plan.

bullets.title: Databricks' Lakebase hits ~$100M ARR within months of launch; governance bottlenecks slowing enterprise AI to production
bullets.body: At Citi's TMT Conference, Databricks highlighted that enterprises remain in early AI deployment stages, with governance and compliance requirements as the primary constraint on moving AI to production. Lakebase reached approximately $100M ARR within months of launch and is growing rapidly. Open-weight model adoption is increasing on economics, and enterprise model routing on open models is rising materially.

bullets.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Financial Services with GPT-6 Astra; integrates LSEG, FactSet, S&P data
bullets.body: OpenAI announced ChatGPT for Financial Services, built on GPT-6 Astra reasoning, with integrations spanning LSEG, FactSet, S&P Capital IQ, MSCI, Moody's, PitchBook, and Daloopa. The product was shaped in design partnership with Morgan Stanley and Evercore, and includes 50+ connectors. Amazon also separately partnered with OpenAI to allow advertisers to run ads within ChatGPT.

bullets.title: Mag 7 outperformed into the close; semis, homebuilders, and unprofitable tech lagged
bullets.body: Into the final 60 minutes of trading, SPX futures led NDX and RTY, with Mag 7 stocks outperforming the broader tape while semiconductors, homebuilders, and unprofitable tech names lagged. Internet and hotel/cruise lines were among the leading subsectors; materials underperformed within the S&P 500. SPX futures were expected to close in the 7,590-7,617 range.
